deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building the Hilbert-space theory of exterior powers. Here \hat\Lambda^n E is the completed n-th exterior power of a Hilbert space E, and u -> \Lambda^n u = u\wedge...\wedge u. Proposition 1, on the previous page, says this map is continuous, multiplicative and *-compatible, with norm at most ||u||^n.

Proposition 2: if u is a compact operator on E with eigenvalues (\lambda_i), then \Lambda^n u is compact on \hat\Lambda^n E. Its eigenvalue sequence is exactly the products \lambda_{i_1}...\lambda_{i_n}, i_1<...<i_n, counted with algebraic multiplicity.

Proof of compactness: u -> \Lambda^n u is continuous in norm and sends finite-rank operators to finite-rank operators. A compact u on Hilbert space is a norm limit of finite-rank operators, so \Lambda^n u is too, hence compact.

Proof of the spectral statement, finite-rank case first. Split E orthogonally as E_0 \oplus E_1 with E_1 finite-dimensional, u(E) \subset E_1 and u|E_0 = 0. One natural choice is E_1 = u(E)+u^*(E) and E_0 = ker u \cap ker u^*. Then use the algebraic isomorphism \Lambda E = \sum_p \Lambda^p E_0 \otimes \Lambda E_1. Grothendieck checks it is compatible with the multiplicative (algebra) structures, and on the next page with the pre-Hilbert structures, as an orthogonal decomposition \hat\Lambda^n E = \sum_{p+q=n} \Lambda^p E_0 \otimes \Lambda^q E_1. With respect to it, \Lambda^n u kills every summand containing a factor from the subspace u annihilates. So the nonzero spectrum of \Lambda^n u is that of \Lambda^n of the finite-dimensional restriction, where the eigenvalue statement is classical linear algebra (triangularization).

The general compact case would then follow by approximation plus continuity of eigenvalues with multiplicities. The next page seems to start on this, mentioning multiplicities and 'distinct' indices.

Purpose: this is groundwork for Fredholm determinants and eigenvalue estimates (Weyl-type inequalities, \prod|\lambda_i| \le \prod s_i) for nuclear and p-summing operators. That material was later published in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956) and the Mémoire 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955).
errors: The transcription's description of E_0, E_1 is internally inconsistent: 'u s'annule sur E_0, u(E) ⊂ E_1' on this page versus 'u(E_1)=0, u(E_0) ⊂ E_0' on the next page. A correct version: E_1 = u(E)+u*(E) (finite-dimensional) and E_0 = its orthogonal, so u is block-diagonal with u|E_0 = 0. An 'intersection of iterated images' (Fitting-type) subspace would not in general have an invariant orthogonal complement.

Gap: passing from finite rank to general compact u requires continuity of the eigenvalue sequence (with algebraic multiplicities) under norm limits of compact operators. This is true via Riesz projections / upper semicontinuity of the spectrum, but it is not proved on this page.
'Exactement' needs a convention on zero eigenvalues and on algebraic versus geometric multiplicity. The statement is correct for nonzero eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity.

ideas.what: Exterior power of a compact operator on Hilbert space is compact, with eigenvalues the n-fold products λ_{i1}…λ_{in}, i1<…<in
ideas.modern_name: Spectrum of antisymmetric tensor powers; tool behind Weyl's inequality and Fredholm determinants
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl (1949), also Horn, Ky Fan; standard in Gohberg–Krein and Simon's 'Trace ideals'
ideas.where_published: La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956); Produits tensoriels topologiques (Mem. AMS 1955), sections on Fredholm determinants and eigenvalues

ideas.what: Compactness of Λ^n u via norm continuity of u→Λ^n u and preservation of finite rank
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of completed exterior powers on Hilbert space

ideas.what: Orthogonal decomposition \hat\Lambda^n(E_0⊕E_1) = ⊕_{p+q=n} Λ^p E_0 ⊗ Λ^q E_1, compatible with algebra and Hilbert structures
ideas.modern_name: Exponential property of the exterior (fermionic Fock) algebra

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard draft details for Hilbert-space exterior powers, serving Grothendieck's Fredholm-theory work, which was published. The results are classical (Weyl 1949), and the page adds nothing beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: Header likely reads 'A voir' in red over a struck-through 'à mettre avant …', followed by 'Notes sur les opérateurs dans les [espaces de] Hilbert'.
'l'intersection des images itérées' is doubtful; the mathematics suggests something like the sum of u(E) and u*(E) (or 'l'image'), with E_0 its orthogonal.
'donc u invariant E_0' is more plausibly 'donc u invariante E_0' / 'laisse invariant E_1'.
The tensor symbols in the sums are \hat\Lambda (completed exterior powers), with the sum over 0≤p≤n: \hat\Lambda E = Σ \hat\Lambda^p E_0 ⊗ \hat\Lambda E_1.
